title: Wikipedia Category Pull: End-to-End Collection & Enrichment
purpose: Standard operating procedure for collecting, extracting, summarizing, tagging, scoring, and indexing all pages from any Wikipedia Category page. Designed to minimize WebSearch usage — only used for article summaries when DBpedia lacks coverage.
trigger: User provides a Wikipedia Category:[Category Name]

phases: Phase 1: Discover all pages in the category (WebFetch, 1 request)
Phase 2: Extract links and metadata via DBpedia SPARQL (no WebSearch)
Phase 3: Write summaries via DBpedia Lookup + WebSearch fallback
Phase 4: Tag, score, categorize, and build indexes (no WebSearch)

websearch_usage.phase_1: NONE — use WebFetch on PetScan or category page
websearch_usage.phase_3: MINIMAL — only for articles not in DBpedia Lookup (typically <40%)

phase_1_discover_pages.title: Phase 1: Discover All Pages in Category
phase_1_discover_pages.goal: Get a complete list of article titles and URLs from the Wikipedia category
phase_1_discover_pages.method: PetScan API (preferred) or WebFetch on the category page

steps.action: Use WebFetch on PetScan to get all pages in the category
steps.note: depth=0 gets only direct pages, not subcategories. Increase depth if subcategories are wanted.

steps.action: Parse the response to extract page titles
steps.detail: PetScan returns JSON with page IDs and titles. Convert titles to Wikipedia URL format: spaces → underscores.

steps.action: Create the data directory and category-pages.json
steps.detail: Directory: storage/sources/wikipedia-{category_slug}/ with cache/, text-cache/, enriched/ subdirectories

phase_1_discover_pages.fallback: If PetScan is down, use WebFetch on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:{CategoryName} and parse the page list from the HTML.

phase_2_extract_links.title: Phase 2: Extract Links and Metadata via DBpedia SPARQL
phase_2_extract_links.goal: Collect external links, internal wiki links, and metadata for every article. NO WebSearch.

steps.action: Initialize WikipediaTools with the new data directory
steps.code:
python3 -c "
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '.')
from storage.scripts.wikipedia_tools import WikipediaTools
wt = WikipediaTools(data_dir='storage/sources/wikipedia-{slug}/')
titles = [p['url'].split('/wiki/')[-1] for p in __import__('json').load(open('storage/sources/wikipedia-{slug}/category-pages.json'))['pages']]
print(f'Loaded {len(titles)} titles')
"

steps.detail: Queries DBpedia SPARQL in batches of 40. Rate limited at 0.5s between batches. Results cached to cache/ext_*.json and cache/int_*.json.

steps.action: Batch extract metadata (categories, descriptions, seeAlso, hypernym)
steps.detail: Queries DBpedia SPARQL in batches of 15. Results cached to cache/meta_*.json.
Check how many articles have links/metadata. Articles missing from DBpedia will have empty arrays — this is expected for newer articles.

phase_2_extract_links.note: Some articles won't exist in DBpedia (newer/obscure). Their cache files will contain empty arrays []. This is handled in Phase 3 and Phase 4.

phase_3_write_summaries.title: Phase 3: Write Article Summaries
phase_3_write_summaries.goal: Get a text summary for every article. Minimize WebSearch — use DBpedia Lookup first.

steps.action: Fetch descriptions from DBpedia Lookup API (no WebSearch)
steps.detail: Hits lookup.dbpedia.org for short descriptions (100-200 chars). Fast, no rate limiting concerns.

steps.action: Check gaps — which articles still need full summaries
steps.detail: Lists articles without text in text-cache/. Typically 30-60% will need WebSearch fallback.

steps.action: Fill gaps with WebSearch (only for missing articles)
steps.detail: For articles not covered by DBpedia Lookup, use WebSearch as fallback. This is the ONLY step that uses WebSearch.

agent_strategy.description: Split missing articles across 2-3 agents. Each agent uses WebSearch to find the Wikipedia article summary, then stores it.
agent_strategy.rate_limit: 2s between WebSearch queries to avoid throttling
agent_strategy.agent_instruction: For each article: WebSearch '{Article_Title} Wikipedia', extract the first 1-3 paragraph summary, store via wiki_text_extractor.py store command

steps.minimization: Only articles missing from DBpedia Lookup are searched. Typically saves 50-70% of WebSearch calls vs searching everything.

phase_4_tag_and_index.title: Phase 4: Tag, Score, Categorize, and Build Indexes
phase_4_tag_and_index.goal: Enrich every article and build master indexes. NO WebSearch — purely local data.

steps.action: Define category taxonomy for this collection
steps.detail: Review a sample of article titles/summaries and define 8-15 categories relevant to the topic. Use the AI category set as a template but adapt to the specific domain.
template_categories: Core Concepts — foundational theory and definitions
Policy & Society — regulation, social impact, ethics
Niche / Low-Value — peripheral, stubs, sparse data

steps.action: Run parallel tagger agents (3 agents recommended)
steps.detail: Split article list into 3 equal batches. Each agent reads text + meta + link files and writes enriched JSON.
steps.agent_instruction: For each article, read text_*.json, meta_*.json, ext_*.json, int_*.json. Compute usefulness score using the rubric. Assign tags, categories, and research tier. Write enriched JSON to enriched/{ID}.json.

enriched_file_schema.title: Human-readable title
int_links: full array of internal wiki link IDs
related_articles: IDs of related articles in collection

steps.action: Run assembler agent to build master indexes
steps.detail: After all taggers complete, one agent builds 3 index files.

index.json.description: Master article index sorted by usefulness score
index.json.contents: All articles with id, title, tags, categories, score, tier, link counts. Plus aggregate summaries (tier counts, category counts, tag counts).

links-index.json.contents: Every external URL and internal wiki link across all articles, deduplicated, with arrays of which articles reference each link. External links include extracted domain. Internal links include is_in_collection flag.

categories.json.contents: Each category with description, article count, and articles sorted by usefulness score.

steps.message_template: Add {CategoryName} Wikipedia category: {N} pages with links and metadata
Add enriched article files for {CategoryName} ({N} articles tagged/scored)
Add master indexes for {CategoryName}: article index, links registry, category taxonomy

output_directory_structure.description: Final directory structure after a complete category pull

enriched/.{ID}.json: Full enriched article with tags, score, links, pointers (Phase 4)

recommended_team.phase_3: 2-3 agents (WebSearch for gap-filling, split by batch)
recommended_team.phase_4: 3 tagger agents (parallel) + 1 assembler agent (sequential after taggers)

agent_team_structure.communication: No inter-agent communication needed — each phase reads the previous phase's output files

websearch_budget.description: Expected WebSearch usage per category pull
websearch_budget.example_234_articles: ~70-140 WebSearch calls total (vs 234+ if searching everything)
optimization_tips: Always run DBpedia Lookup first — it covers 40-70% of articles
Batch WebSearch gap-filling across parallel agents for speed
Cache aggressively — subsequent runs are nearly instant

quick_reference.title: Quick Reference: Run a Category Pull
steps: 7. python3 storage/scripts/wiki_text_extractor.py gaps → fill with WebSearch agents

procedures: Phase 1: Discover pages via PetScan API (WebFetch, no WebSearch)
Phase 2: Extract links/metadata via DBpedia SPARQL (wikipedia_tools.py batch)
Phase 3: Write summaries via DBpedia Lookup + WebSearch fallback for gaps only
Phase 4: Tag, score, categorize with parallel tagger agents, build master indexes
Phase 5: Commit and push with structured commit messages
